source: Researched profiles synthesised from the 5 Dec 2025 Final Draw, 31 Mar 2026 playoff results, late-2025/early-2026 FIFA World Ranking direction, qualifying-cycle form, and squad knowledge to ~Jan 2026. Contender-tier modelRatings recalibrated 10 Jun 2026 to the pre-tournament betting-market consensus (FOX Sports/ESPN outright odds): Spain & France out front, England clear third, Brazil > Argentina, Germany above the Netherlands, Colombia/Japan lifted, Croatia faded. Re-verify squads after FIFA confirms final lists on 2 Jun 2026.

profiles.recentForm: Won the 2025 Gold Cup; results uneven in friendlies but lifted at home venues.
profiles.worldCupPedigree: 18th appearance; perennial last-16 side chasing a first deep run since 1986.
weaknesses: Goal threat dependent on Gimenez form
profiles.narrative: A host with a real environment edge and a settled spine, finally chasing the seventh game it has never reached.

profiles.recentForm: Topped a tricky CAF group; bronze at AFCON 2023 showed knockout bite.
profiles.worldCupPedigree: Third appearance; still seeking a first knockout-stage berth.
weaknesses: Finishing can dry up in tight games
profiles.narrative: A quick, front-foot outsider whose path depends on turning the tight games AFCON proved it can win.

profiles.recentForm: Comfortable through AFC qualifying; reliable results under a structured setup.
profiles.worldCupPedigree: 12th appearance; 2002 semi-finalists and regular knockout contenders.
weaknesses: Can be opened up by top-end attacking talent
profiles.narrative: An experienced, well-led side with enough quality through the spine to make any group game uncomfortable.

profiles.recentForm: Survived the playoffs to qualify; disciplined if unspectacular in the run-in.
profiles.worldCupPedigree: First as Czechia since 2006; Czechoslovak/Czech runs include Euro 96 final and 1962 WC final.
weaknesses: Can lack a creative gear in open play
profiles.narrative: A disciplined, set-piece-driven side that earned its place the hard way and can upset a complacent seed.

profiles.recentForm: Reached the 2024 Copa America semis under Jesse Marsch; trending upward at home.
profiles.worldCupPedigree: Third appearance; chasing a first-ever World Cup win after a winless 2022.
profiles.narrative: An athletic host trending sharply upward, with Davies and David giving it a genuine ceiling on home soil.

profiles.recentForm: Came through the UEFA playoffs; competitive but streaky in qualifying.
profiles.worldCupPedigree: Second appearance after a 2014 debut group exit.
strengths: Veteran know-how through Dzeko and Pjanic
profiles.narrative: A technical European outsider leaning on veteran quality; its ceiling depends on controlling midfield.

profiles.recentForm: Back-to-back Asian Cup winners (2023); strong in the regional bubble.
profiles.worldCupPedigree: Second appearance; lost all three as 2022 hosts, seeking a first WC point.
weaknesses: Step up from Asian to World Cup level
profiles.narrative: Twice Asian champions but yet to prove it on the World stage; needs low-margin games to break its way.

profiles.recentForm: Reached the Euro 2024 quarter-finals; consistently grinds out results.
profiles.worldCupPedigree: 13th appearance; regular qualifiers who reached the 2022 last 16.
weaknesses: Can lack cutting edge in open games
Reliant on a tight defensive base
profiles.narrative: A reliable tournament operator that rarely beats itself and carries a strong floor against most group opponents.

profiles.recentForm: Steadied under Carlo Ancelotti late in qualifying after a wobbly cycle.
profiles.worldCupPedigree: Record 23rd appearance; five-time champions (last 2002), the only ever-present nation.
profiles.narrative: Ancelotti has tightened a star-laden squad; the pedigree and forward line make Brazil a threat to win any tie.

profiles.recentForm: Dominant in CAF qualifying; carrying momentum from a 2022 semi-final run.
profiles.worldCupPedigree: Seventh appearance; 2022 fourth place, the best-ever African finish.
profiles.narrative: The best African side of its generation: organised, athletic and battle-tested, with genuine deep-run credibility.

profiles.recentForm: Edged a dramatic CONCACAF path; results swing on individual moments.
profiles.worldCupPedigree: Second appearance, first since 1974.
weaknesses: Depth and experience against top-tier sides
profiles.narrative: A romantic returnee after 52 years; its route to a shock runs through chaos, dead balls and clinical finishing.

profiles.recentForm: Qualified from a strong group; physical and well-organised under Steve Clarke.
profiles.worldCupPedigree: Ninth appearance, first since 1998; never past the group stage.
weaknesses: Limited cutting edge against deep defences
profiles.narrative: Back after 28 years and desperate to clear the group-stage barrier; awkward and physical when matches stay tight.

profiles.recentForm: Mixed under Mauricio Pochettino, but building cohesion ahead of a home World Cup.
profiles.worldCupPedigree: 12th appearance; 2002 quarter-finalists, last-16 in 2022.
profiles.narrative: A young, European-honed core with a home crowd; if Pochettino unlocks the front line the ceiling is a deep run.

profiles.recentForm: Surged late under Gustavo Alfaro to seal qualification; hard to break down.
profiles.worldCupPedigree: Ninth appearance, first since 2010; reached the 2010 quarter-finals.
weaknesses: Can struggle when forced to lead the play
profiles.narrative: A rugged Alfaro side that returns after 16 years; its model value rises in low-scoring, physical matches.

profiles.recentForm: Steady through AFC qualifying; durable and well-drilled under Tony Popovic.
profiles.worldCupPedigree: Seventh appearance; reached the last 16 in 2006 and 2022.
profiles.narrative: A durable, well-coached side that habitually keeps itself alive deep into groups and punishes lapses on set plays.

profiles.recentForm: Reached the Euro 2024 quarter-finals; talented but volatile in the playoffs.
profiles.worldCupPedigree: Sixth appearance, first since 2002, when it finished third.
strengths: Technical attacking quality and high ceiling
profiles.narrative: A gifted young side with a ceiling far above its pot; if the temperament holds it can embarrass bigger names.

profiles.recentForm: Resurgent under Julian Nagelsmann after a home Euro 2024 quarter-final.
profiles.worldCupPedigree: 21st appearance; four-time champions, though group exits in 2018 and 2022.
strengths: Technical control and a golden midfield generation
profiles.narrative: A heavyweight rebuilt around Wirtz and Musiala, aiming to bury two shock group exits with a real title tilt.

profiles.recentForm: Punched above its weight to top a CONCACAF group; tight, well-drilled games.
profiles.worldCupPedigree: Tournament debut; the smallest nation by population ever to qualify.
weaknesses: Squad depth across a long tournament
profiles.narrative: A landmark debutant of Dutch-Caribbean talent; its best route is to defend deep and steal one decisive moment.

profiles.recentForm: Built on a home 2023 AFCON title; confident and athletic in qualifying.
profiles.worldCupPedigree: Fourth appearance; never past the group stage despite golden-era squads.
strengths: Winning mentality from the AFCON triumph
weaknesses: History of underperforming at World Cups
profiles.narrative: Reigning African champions with the athleticism to trouble any seed; the question is converting that into a first knockout berth.

profiles.recentForm: Finished high in CONMEBOL with the best defensive record in the region.
profiles.worldCupPedigree: Fifth appearance; reached the last 16 in 2006.
profiles.narrative: A young, athletic side with an elite midfield and the best defence in qualifying; a serious dark horse to advance.

profiles.recentForm: Euro 2024 semi-finalists; consistent under Ronald Koeman.
profiles.worldCupPedigree: 12th appearance; three-time runners-up still chasing a first title.
profiles.narrative: A top seed with van Dijk anchoring a structured, talented side; finishing is the variable between good and great.

profiles.recentForm: Demolished AFC qualifying, the first nation to book its place; flying form.
profiles.worldCupPedigree: Eighth appearance; four straight last-16 exits, chasing a first quarter-final.
strengths: Cohesion and depth of European-based talent
profiles.narrative: Asia's standout, fast and superbly drilled; this may be the deepest squad yet to finally break the round-of-16 barrier.

profiles.recentForm: Stuttered in the group but came through the playoffs; firepower remains.
profiles.worldCupPedigree: 13th appearance, first since 2018, when it reached the quarter-finals.
strengths: Two elite strikers and set-piece threat
profiles.narrative: A fourth-pot side carrying two of Europe's best strikers; if the supply line clicks it can wreck a group.

profiles.recentForm: Cruised through a CAF group unbeaten; disciplined and compact.
profiles.worldCupPedigree: Seventh appearance; never advanced past the group stage.
weaknesses: Struggles to create when forced to attack
profiles.narrative: Best when games stay tight and defensive discipline can carry the result; a stubborn out for any favourite.

profiles.recentForm: Topped qualifying as a golden generation transitions to youth.
profiles.worldCupPedigree: 15th appearance; 2018 third place remains the high-water mark.
strengths: High-end attacking quality and De Bruyne's craft
Pace and depth in wide areas
profiles.narrative: Still a heavyweight on talent, blending De Bruyne's vintage with young pace; the back line is the open question.

profiles.recentForm: Strolled through a CAF group; results lean heavily on Salah's output.
profiles.worldCupPedigree: Fourth appearance; yet to win a World Cup match since 1934 until 1990, no knockout berth.
weaknesses: Depth and chance control beyond the stars
profiles.narrative: As far as Salah and Marmoush can carry it; a decisive attack could finally drag Egypt into the knockouts.

profiles.recentForm: Qualified early and comfortably; organised and hard to beat.
profiles.worldCupPedigree: Seventh appearance; record without ever reaching the knockout stage.
strengths: Genuine goal threat in Taremi and Azmoun
weaknesses: Carrying a chance into a first knockout berth
profiles.narrative: A tough, organised side with real strikers that habitually keeps matches closer than the ratings imply.

profiles.recentForm: Dominant in Oceania as expected; rarely tested at a high level.
profiles.worldCupPedigree: Third appearance; unbeaten yet eliminated in the group in 2010.
strengths: Set pieces and aerial threat through Wood
weaknesses: Big step up in opponent quality
profiles.narrative: A clear underdog whose upset path runs through dead balls, Wood's finishing and keeping the score low.

profiles.recentForm: European champions in 2024, then Nations League finalists; the form team of world football.
profiles.worldCupPedigree: 17th appearance; 2010 world champions.
strengths: Elite possession control and chance suppression
Best young attacking talent in the world
weaknesses: Finishing can lag the volume of chances
profiles.narrative: The world's top-ranked side and a deserved favourite; relentless control plus Yamal's brilliance make it the team to beat.

profiles.recentForm: Stunned its CAF group to top it; the feel-good story of qualifying.
profiles.worldCupPedigree: Tournament debut; one of the smallest nations ever to qualify.
weaknesses: Squad depth over a long tournament
profiles.narrative: A landmark debutant punching far above its size; a plausible spoiler if matches become narrow and physical.

profiles.recentForm: Ground out qualification; defensively cautious under a pragmatic setup.
profiles.worldCupPedigree: Seventh appearance; famously beat eventual champions Argentina in 2022.
weaknesses: Limited away from the regional bubble
profiles.narrative: A side with shock pedigree and a quality wide threat, but its model still demands disciplined, low-event defending.

profiles.recentForm: Strong under Marcelo Bielsa; high-pressing and intense in qualifying.
profiles.worldCupPedigree: 15th appearance; two-time champions and 2010 semi-finalists.
strengths: Bielsa's intensity and a CONMEBOL edge
profiles.narrative: A pedigreed, hard-running Bielsa side whose intensity travels; a genuine threat to reach the latter stages.

profiles.recentForm: Comfortable in qualifying; reached the Euro 2024 semis and the 2022 WC final.
profiles.worldCupPedigree: 17th appearance; two-time champions and 2022 runners-up.
strengths: Elite squad depth at every position
Mbappe's match-winning ceiling and recent pedigree
weaknesses: Reliance on Mbappe to unlock tight games
profiles.narrative: A perennial favourite where depth, athleticism and pedigree all point the same way; built to win it again.

profiles.recentForm: Topped its CAF group; powerful and consistent since the 2021 AFCON title.
profiles.worldCupPedigree: Fourth appearance; reached the quarter-finals in 2002 and last 16 in 2022.
strengths: Physicality and athleticism across the pitch
Recent African pedigree and a strong spine
profiles.narrative: One of Africa's powerhouses: athletic, experienced and physically dominant enough to pressure any favourite.

profiles.recentForm: Edged the inter-confederation playoff; momentum but limited margin.
profiles.worldCupPedigree: Second appearance, first since 1986; 2007 Asian Cup champions.
strengths: Momentum from a hard-won playoff path
weaknesses: Creating clear chances at this level
profiles.narrative: A long-awaited returnee whose best path is disciplined, low-event football and capitalising on rare openings.

profiles.recentForm: Stormed through qualifying with a prolific record; Haaland in vintage form.
profiles.worldCupPedigree: Fourth appearance, first since 1998; never past the last 16.
profiles.narrative: Back after 28 years with Haaland and Odegaard in their prime; an attacking force that can break any model on its day.

profiles.recentForm: Dominated CONMEBOL qualifying; Copa America 2024 champions and reigning world champions.
profiles.worldCupPedigree: 19th appearance; three-time champions and defending holders.
weaknesses: Cycle-age questions around Messi and the core
profiles.narrative: The reigning champions with unmatched tournament know-how and a very high floor; built to defend the crown.

profiles.recentForm: Topped its CAF group comfortably; technically gifted and confident.
profiles.worldCupPedigree: Fifth appearance; reached the last 16 in 2014.
strengths: Creative control through Bennacer and Mahrez
weaknesses: Can be passive without the ball
profiles.narrative: A technically rich side that can dictate group games; if the defence holds, it has the talent for a deep run.

profiles.recentForm: Impressed at Euro 2024 and topped its qualifying group; intense and structured.
profiles.worldCupPedigree: Eighth appearance, first since 1998; 1954 third place its peak.
profiles.narrative: A Rangnick-drilled pressing machine that rates above a typical pot-three side; a dark horse to escape its group strongly.

profiles.recentForm: Qualified for the first time after a 2023 Asian Cup final run; rising belief.
profiles.worldCupPedigree: Tournament debut.
profiles.narrative: A debutant riding its Asian Cup-final surge; its route to points is compact defending and sharp counters.

profiles.recentForm: Won the 2025 Nations League; deep, talented and confident under Roberto Martinez.
profiles.worldCupPedigree: Ninth appearance; 2006 semi-finalists, golden-generation depth.
strengths: Elite attacking depth and midfield control
profiles.narrative: A loaded squad with Nations League silverware and arguably its best midfield ever; a genuine contender to go all the way.

profiles.recentForm: Came through the inter-confederation playoff; athletic and improving.
profiles.worldCupPedigree: Second appearance, first since 1974 (as Zaire).
strengths: Playoff momentum and a strong AFCON pedigree
profiles.narrative: A powerful, athletic returnee after a half-century; upset tools are there, but the model margin is thin.

profiles.recentForm: Qualified directly for the first time; a rising, well-coached generation.
profiles.worldCupPedigree: Tournament debut.
profiles.narrative: A debutant with genuine upward momentum and a more credible baseline than pure novelty suggests.

profiles.recentForm: Strong qualifying campaign after reaching the 2024 Copa America final.
profiles.worldCupPedigree: Seventh appearance; 2014 quarter-finalists.
strengths: James pulling strings behind Diaz's threat
weaknesses: Can be pulled into chaotic game states
profiles.narrative: A Copa America finalist with elite attacking talent; the qualifying environment gives the model real confidence in it.

profiles.recentForm: Perfect or near-perfect qualifying under Thomas Tuchel after a 2024 Euros final.
profiles.worldCupPedigree: 17th appearance; 1966 champions, 2018 semi-finalists, 2022 quarter-finalists.
strengths: Elite attacking options and squad depth
profiles.narrative: A top favourite under Tuchel with a star-laden squad and recent deep runs; finally favoured to convert pedigree into a trophy.

profiles.recentForm: Comfortable in qualifying; veteran-led and tournament-savvy.
profiles.worldCupPedigree: Seventh appearance; 2018 runners-up and 2022 third place.
strengths: Midfield control and serial deep-run pedigree
weaknesses: Ageing core and pace through the spine
profiles.narrative: Two straight World Cup podiums say never write them off; Modric's last dance, built on control rather than legs.

profiles.recentForm: Topped its CAF group to bounce back from a poor AFCON; volatile but talented.
profiles.worldCupPedigree: Fifth appearance; 2010 quarter-finalists, the agonising near-miss.
strengths: Athletic transitions and a star in Kudus
profiles.narrative: A volatile side with pace, history and Kudus's spark; enough to make any favourite nervous on a good day.

profiles.recentForm: Reached the 2023 Gold Cup final and 2025 latter stages; physical and improving.
profiles.worldCupPedigree: Second appearance, first since a winless 2018 debut.
weaknesses: Cutting edge in the final third
profiles.narrative: A hard-working, improving CONCACAF outsider whose best route is keeping matches close and ugly.
